title: Potential Benefits and Risks of Artificial Intelligence in Education
venue: Bartın University Journal of Faculty of Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines the potential benefits and risks of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, with particular attention to the rapid spread of generative AI systems such as ChatGPT. The central question is how AI systems may support teaching, learning, assessment, and educational administration, while also creating ethical, privacy, bias, and equity concerns. The author positions the paper as a systematic review of prior studies and reports, using document analysis to synthesize relevant literature across educational contexts.

Rather than evaluating a single intervention, the paper surveys the broader landscape of AI uses in education. It discusses teacher-facing uses such as lesson planning, creating instructional materials, assessment support, grading, and feedback generation, as well as student-facing uses such as assignment support, translation, and personalized learning. The paper also includes school and policy-level uses, such as decision-making and educational management. The discussion explicitly distinguishes assistive teacher tools and intelligent tutoring / automated assessment systems from student misuse of generative text tools, emphasizing that AI may support instruction but should not replace teachers.

The paper is not based on a primary empirical sample; instead, it synthesizes claims from the literature to identify recurring opportunities and risks. It concludes that AI can reduce workload, personalize learning, and improve feedback and assessment processes, but may also intensify inequality, undermine academic integrity, reproduce bias, and create privacy and data-protection problems. The author recommends responsible AI use, stronger AI literacy for students, teachers, and administrators, updated teacher preparation and in-service training, and more robust assessment practices that can detect unethical use and better capture student learning.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot/large language model system used for conversational text generation, question answering, and support tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discusses ChatGPT as an example of generative AI in education, including teacher uses such as lesson planning, preparing materials, creating exams, conducting assessments, providing feedback, and generating interactive learning scenarios; it also notes student use for assignments and exams.

findings.finding_summary: This systematic review reports that ChatGPT can support teachers with lesson planning, material generation, exam creation, assessment, feedback, and interactive learning scenarios, and can also help students with assignments, presentations, translation, and access to materials. The paper does not report original effect sizes or study-level estimates; it synthesizes potential benefits and risks from prior literature.
findings.measure: Narrative review of reported educational uses, benefits, and risks

findings.finding_summary: The review emphasizes risks including privacy and data protection concerns, academic integrity/plagiarism, bias in outputs, unequal access, and potential teacher workload increases or role displacement. It argues that uncritical use may deepen inequities and weaken assessment validity, but no quantitative estimates are provided.
findings.measure: Narrative review of reported risks and policy concerns

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review and policy-oriented discussion rather than an empirical evaluation of a single intervention. No original experimental design, effect sizes, or quantitative outcome estimates are reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially substantial educational relevance for teacher workflow, assessment, and literacy instruction, but it provides no measured effect sizes. The impact is therefore conceptually meaningful yet empirically unquantified.
